## Overview

LRP77a is the **baseline-ability sensitivity fit** for [LRP77](../lrp-rli-dose-077/). It is
the identical dose-response model with the **baseline-skill cluster** added to the
adjustment set: letter-sound knowledge ($L$), expressive vocabulary ($E$) and
phoneme blending ($B$). These are the reflective indicators of latent general
ability $g$ in the revised DAG, alongside the already-adjusted baseline reading
$W_{\text{pre}}$.

**Each adjuster is that child's verified t1 value, broadcast across all three
transitions.** This matters more than it sounds. Until #587 the fit used each
transition's *own* starting wave — t1 skills in period 1, but t2 skills in period
2 and t3 skills in period 3. Those later values are themselves downstream of
earlier intervention and attendance, so the model was conditioning on a
treatment-affected time-varying covariate rather than on a baseline: it could
block part of the very path it was measuring, and it was not the
pre-randomisation ability adjustment it was published as. The repair changes 98 of
the 156 fitted rows' ability values. `ability_baseline_wave="transition_start"`
retains the old behaviour as an explicitly labelled comparator; it must not be
read as a baseline sensitivity.

**Why.** The revised DAG carries $GA \to IS$ (latent), so if abler children
attended more (Frank 2012) then $g$ is a common cause of attendance and outcome
and the measured adjustment set does not identify an attendance effect — and
because attendance is **not** randomised, randomisation does not rescue it.
Conditioning on the baseline-skill cluster probes that path with observed proxies.

**How to read it — against LRP77.** If the attendance slope is materially
unchanged here, the assumption that ability does not drive attendance is more
defensible in this sample. If it collapses toward zero, the LRP77 signal is
substantially ability-confounded and should be downgraded. **Neither outcome
proves the latent path is closed:** these are noisy proxies for $g$, not $g$.

See the LRP77 report for the full estimand, the extensive/intensive split, the
$G = 2 - \text{group}$ coding (G=1 = intervention), and the expectations caveat
(adjusted association; $R^2$ 0.1–0.3 in Phase 1).
